Nike had increasingly leaned on Mbappé as one of the ⁠sport's leading global ambassadors following the latter stages of soccer star Cristiano Ronaldo's career. The World Cup winner remained a centerpiece of Nike's football marketing at this year's FIFA World Cup, most recently receiving signature editions of its ‌Mercurial boots. headline: JUTC to revise lugage management system
snippet: THE Jamaica Urban Transit Company (JUTC) said it is reviewing the company’s bag policy to enhance luggage management following a recent article that reported a passenger onboard an express bus from Kingston to Montego Bay, St James, lost a bag containing approximately US$2,000 ($315,000) worth of special educational tools and other items. The passenger, a special education teacher, said that she boarded the express bus with five bags on September 1, but only saw four of her bags when she arrived in Montego Bay and went to retrieve the items. In a release on Thursday, the company responded to the Jamaica Observer article, stating that investigations revealed that the bag was left at the Half-Way-Tree Transport Centre prior to the passengers’ departure, and was not lost in transit. The company said the bag was located and placed in the custody of security personnel. According to the JUTC, the bag is currently being stored in a guard house pending its collection by the owner, who has already been contacted and advised to make arrangements to verify and collect the luggage in question. “The JUTC wishes to first acknowledge the distress and inconvenience expressed by the passenger. We understand the importance of the items described and appreciate the frustration that can arise when a passenger believes that personal belongings have been lost while using public transportation,” the company said in a release. The company noted that its policy states that, “passengers transport luggage and other personal belongings at their own risk and the company does not accept liability for loss or damage to such property in accordance with its stated terms and conditions”. However, that policy is now being reviewed. “The JUTC recognises that the incident highlights an opportunity to further strengthen its processes for the handling and identification of passenger luggage, particularly on longer-distance and express services. Accordingly, the company is reviewing measures to enhance luggage management and passenger accountability, including the potential implementation of passenger, baggage and/or luggage tagging systems, together with strengthened procedures for the handling and recording of unclaimed or left-behind items at JUTC facilities,” the release said. The company further reiterated its commitment to delivering safe, reliable, and customer-focused public transportation services. “We value passenger feedback and will continue to use such feedback to identify gaps, strengthen our systems, and improve the overall passenger experience. The company regrets the distress and inconvenience experienced by the passenger and remains committed to resolving matters of this nature in a professional, fair, and transparent manner,” it added.

headline: Staehr first winner on new marathon course
snippet: More than 300 participants took to the Wimmera River trails in Horsham on Sunday September 13 as part of the second annual Horsham Running Festival. Residents and intrastate and interstate travellers competed in the marathon, half marathon, quarter marathon or 5km event, with youngsters competing in the 2km dash. Event organiser Brian Haddy said it was good to have runners of various abilities take to the occasion, acknowledging numerous milestones, including marathon winner David Staehr from Kaniva. "David won it for the second successive year and has won the last nine events my company, Marathon Adventures, has run," Haddy said. "That was his 94th marathon and he's aiming to complete 100 marathons before he turns 50 next year. "One of our marathon pacers, Bryan Lypp, ran his 50th marathon of the year on Sunday, which is extraordinary. "At the other end of the spectrum, we had runners doing their first event or trying a new distance for the first time. "A woman was incredibly nervous at the start of her event but she was so delighted at the finish." Staehr finished the marathon in 2 hours, 47 minutes and 14 seconds, while Louisa Maney was the first female finisher in a time of 3 hours, 57 minutes and 12 seconds. In the half marathon, Tim Davis was the first finisher in 1 hour, 21 minutes and 54 seconds, while Kim Parker was the first female over the line in 1 hour, 44 minutes and 19 seconds. Haddy said the festival would retain this year's changed course, with the event set to count as an official marathon going forward. "We had a new course this year because the Weir Park Boardwalk we used last year was threatening to be either underwater or slippery," he said. "This year you would pass people running the other way for part of the loop, which gave it a bit more of a community feel. "We're going to stick to that course now because we've had it measured by the Association of International Marathons and Distance Races. "So for next year and beyond we'll keep the same course as it means if you run a fast time on that course it will count as a qualifying time for international marathons like Boston and New York." Haddy said going forward he would include the Horsham Running Festival as part of the Western Victoria Marathon Triseries, along with the Dimbooal Dash and Mildura Riverfront Marathon Festival. "Hopefully that will encourage more people to come to all of them and you get a special medal if do all three marathons next year," Haddy said. "Overall numbers were at about 330, which is a touch up from last year, but I think there's plenty of room for further improvement, which I think the triseries inclusion will help with." Full results can be found online at https://my.raceresult.com/415558/

headline: Google Gemini Notebook Gets a Major Upgrade: Here’s What’s New
snippet: Google announced new features for Gemini Notebook, the AI-powered research and study tool previously known as NotebookLM. The update introduces real-time voice conversations, an audio recorder and interactive learning tools such as quizzes and flashcards. The company is also offering eligible college students free access to its paid Google AI plans for one year, with higher usage limits in Gemini Notebook. Real-Time Voice Chats Gemini Notebook will soon let users have real-time spoken conversations with their notebooks through its mobile app on Android, iPhone, and iPad. Google says the feature will work in nearly 100 languages. Users will be able to ask questions, get step-by-step guidance and interrupt the conversation while speaking. Responses will remain grounded in the sources added to the notebook, letting users discuss study material through voice instead of typing questions and reading text responses. The feature is rolling out to Google AI Ultra subscribers aged 18 and above this week, with Google AI Pro subscribers and other users set to get access soon. Audio Recording Google is also adding an audio recorder to the Gemini Notebook mobile app starting next week. Users can record lectures, meetings or their own thoughts directly inside the app. The recordings will become sources in the relevant notebook, alongside documents, handwritten notes, worksheets and photos. Users can then chat with, cite and build from these recordings while continuing to edit their notes. Interactive Study Tools Gemini Notebook is adding interactive learning overviews under Reports, combining summaries with studio content such as infographics, quizzes and flashcards. New quiz formats will include short-answer, multiple-select and fill-in-the-blank questions. Users will also be able to review their quiz and flashcard performance through notebook chat and customise questions. Short Video Overviews are expanding to more than 80 languages, with videos of around 60 seconds combining narration and educational animations.
